notes: Take after Lab 10. Covers importing and configuring antd/MUI components, props, forms, and customization.

questions.question: What is the main benefit of using a component library such as Ant Design (`antd`) or MUI?
options: It makes your app run faster than plain HTML
You get ready-made, consistent, accessible UI components (buttons, forms, carousels, etc.) instead of building and styling each from scratch
It replaces React, so you don't need to learn it
It removes the need to write any CSS or JavaScript
questions.explanation: Component libraries save time and give a consistent look and accessibility features. They are built *on top of* React, and you still write your own logic and layout.

questions.question: You ran `npm install antd`. Which line correctly imports the `Button` and `Carousel` components?
questions.explanation: antd exports each component by name, so use named imports from the package name (`"antd"`).

questions.question:
What are **props** in the following code?

```jsx
<Button type="primary" size="large">Search</Button>
```
options: `type` and `size`: the inputs you pass to configure the component
The CSS file that styles it
questions.explanation: Props are the attributes you give a component. Each library documents the props available (and their allowed values) on every component's page. The text between the tags is the `children` prop.

questions.question: Where should you look first to find out how to make an antd `Input` disabled or to change its size?
options: The component's page in the official docs, specifically the examples and the **API** (props) table
Trial and error with random props
questions.explanation: The docs' API table lists every prop, its type, its default, and what it does. The examples show typical usage you can copy and adapt.

questions.question:
In the antd `Form` below, what is the purpose of `name="q"`?

```jsx
<Form onFinish={handleSubmit}>
    <Form.Item label="Search" name="q">
        <Input />
    </Form.Item>
    <Button htmlType="submit">Go</Button>
</Form>
```
options: It sets the text shown to the user
It is the CSS class for styling
It is the key under which the input's value appears in the object passed to `handleSubmit`, e.g., `{ q: "Beyonce" }`
questions.explanation: `name` links the field to the form's internal data. When the form is submitted, `onFinish` receives an object keyed by each `Form.Item`'s `name`.

questions.question: The antd button in a form does nothing when clicked. Which prop is most likely missing?
questions.explanation: antd's `type` prop controls the *visual* style (`primary`, `dashed`, ...). `htmlType` controls the underlying HTML button type; `submit` is what triggers the form's `onFinish`.

questions.question: Your form has an antd `<InputNumber min={1} max={20} />` named `limit`. What type of value will `values.limit` be in `onFinish`?
questions.explanation: `InputNumber` gives you a number, whereas `Input` gives you a string. This matters when you do math or build a URL.

questions.question: You use antd's `Carousel` and want one slide per item in an array. Which approach follows the pattern from the lab?
questions.explanation: Library components take children. Use `.map()` to turn each data item into a child element, and give each one a unique `key`. `for` loops don't produce values inside JSX.

questions.question: In MUI, how do you typically install the library and use a `Button`?
options: `npm install @mui/material @emotion/react @emotion/styled`, then `import Button from "@mui/material/Button"` (or `import { Button } from "@mui/material"`)
Download a ZIP file and copy it into `src`
questions.explanation: MUI is published as `@mui/material` and needs its styling engine (Emotion) as a peer dependency. The usage pattern is the same as antd's: install, import, then pass props.

questions.question: Which ways can you customize a third-party component's appearance? Select all that apply.
options: Pass built-in props documented for the component (e.g., `size`, `type`)
Use the library's theming option (e.g., antd's `ConfigProvider`, MUI's `ThemeProvider`) to change defaults for the whole app
questions.explanation: Props, `style`/`className`, and theming are the supported ways. Editing `node_modules` is a bad idea because your changes vanish on the next `npm install` and aren't part of your repo.

questions.question: Do you need a `useState` variable for each antd `Form.Item` input to know what the user typed?
options: Yes, antd forms don't work without state for every field
No. The antd `Form` manages the field values for you and gives them to `onFinish` when the form is submitted
No, because React doesn't need state for forms
questions.explanation: antd's `Form` keeps its own internal state. You use `useState` for *your* data, such as the tracks returned from the server, which React needs to know about so it can redraw.

questions.question: What is a real **trade-off** of relying on a third-party component library?
options: Components can't be used with React
You can't change anything about the components
Added dependency and bundle size, a learning curve for the library's API, and your app's look and behavior is constrained by what the library supports
questions.explanation: Libraries speed you up but come with costs: bigger bundles, breaking changes between versions, and limits on customization. Weigh that against the time saved building and testing common components yourself.
